overview: Qin began as a frontier state of the Zhou in the Wei River valley in 770 BCE and grew, by reform and conquest, into the power that unified China in 221 BCE. The empire created a centralized bureaucratic state that replaced feudal fragmentation. Though the dynasty lasted only fifteen years, its institutional innovations became the foundation of all subsequent Chinese empires.

items.text: Shang Yang's reforms in the state of Qin reward farming and soldiering, punish by fixed law and break the power of the old nobility, the Legalist programme the empire would follow.
Legalism becomes state orthodoxy, emphasizing strict laws, harsh punishments and absolute state power.
Books of rival philosophies are ordered burned, and by tradition scholars are executed the next year.
The First Emperor seeks immortality through alchemy and travels to sacred mountains.
Standardization of weights, measures, axle widths and written script across the empire.
Construction of the Great Wall begins, connecting earlier defensive walls along the northern frontier.
The Terracotta Army, some 8,000 life-size soldiers, is completed to guard the First Emperor's tomb; work had begun on his accession in 246 BCE.
Bronze mirrors, crossbow mechanisms and standardized coinage show unified artistic standards.
The small seal script standardized for official use, later replaced by clerical script.
The empire divided into thirty-six commanderies governed by appointed officials rather than hereditary lords.
Corvée labor conscripted for massive public works: roads, the Lingqu canal linking the Yangzi and Pearl river systems, and the Epang palace.
Harsh legal code applied uniformly across the empire.
Standardized bronze coins in round shape with square hole become the empire's currency.
Imperial highways facilitate military movement and commercial exchange.
The name China probably derives from Qin, by way of Sanskrit and Persian.
Centralized bureaucratic administration replaced feudalism in all subsequent dynasties.
Standardized writing enabled cultural unity across linguistic diversity.

fall.text: After the First Emperor's death, popular rebellions and civil war led to the dynasty's collapse in 206 BCE; Liu Bang, the victor of the wars that followed, founded the Han.
